A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAAD study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original adversarial-distillation experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and results over three random seeds.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds controlled comparisons, transferability diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The entropy-weighted SAAD objective, complementary SAAD-C loss, AdaAD/IGDM backbone, teacher approximation, and SWA procedure remain unchanged in Equations 8–9 and Algorithms 2–3. Newly evaluated variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage remains CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and the existing distribution-shift and black-box evaluations. The black-box results moved from v1 Appendix C.7 to v2 Section 5.3; new diagnostic sweeps stay within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the uniform clean-distillation comparator 'SAAD + Clean KD' against SAAD-C in Figure 5 and clean-entropy weighting against SAAD in Table 18. The principal PGD-AT, TRADES, and six distillation baselines are retained.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols sweep training PGD steps and perturbation bounds, evaluate the entropy proxy through ROC/PR curves and entropy bins, and vary AVar training-data splits. These supplement the existing evaluation; the main training schedule, attack settings, and benchmark metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially expands validation of the design: selective versus uniform clean distillation, attack-strength effects on transferability, quantitative entropy-proxy assessment, clean versus adversarial entropy, and AVar estimator sensitivity. These test previously unexamined controls and reliability questions rather than merely redisplaying benchmark scores.

E5.justification: Figure 6 newly reports a correlation coefficient and significance result, r = 0.940 and p < 0.001. Table 21 adds AVar sensitivity configurations with K = 3 and 5 repetitions alongside the existing K = 2 default. Primary three-seed means and standard deviations remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial diagnostic findings, including the clean-KD trade-off curves, entropy-proxy ROC-AUC 0.772 and PR-AUC 0.376, and stable teacher ordering across AVar configurations. Table 18 reports clean-entropy AA accuracy of 47.85% versus SAAD's retained 50.35% for Gowal2021Improving. Original benchmark scores, including the relocated black-box results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The TAS definition, both lemmas and their proofs, bias–variance decomposition, and first-order approximation are retained. v2 qualifies the usefulness of the existing entropy bound without changing its assumptions, statement, or derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction's claim of consistently improving both clean accuracy and robustness becomes a claim of improved robustness with a tunable clean–robustness trade-off. The conclusion adopts this qualification, while the central transferability diagnosis and SAAD contribution remain intact.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3.1 replaces v1's assertion that the bound justifies entropy weighting with an explicit acknowledgment that it can be vacuous for overconfident teachers, making the proxy empirically motivated. Appendix D adds limitations concerning larger datasets and theoretical guarantees, and develops the feature/capacity-mismatch explanation of teacher failures.

D1.justification: v2 documents the unweighted clean-distillation control loss in Equation 33 and supplies parameters for new diagnostic sweeps in Figure 6 and Table 21. Existing optimizer settings, algorithms, hardware/runtime information, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix D adds theoretical connections to margin geometry, robustness–accuracy trade-offs, capacity scaling, and non-robust features, citing additional works such as Charles et al., Javanmard and Soltanolkotabi, and Ilyas et al. The main related-work discussion and positioning within adversarial distillation remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized claim and explanation edits, reorganizes Section 5.3, moves black-box discussion into the main text, and expands Appendix D into limitations, discussion, and future work. Citation style, publication information, and acknowledgments change, but most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document-wide typography and layout, recolors Figure 1 by TAS ratio, and adds Figures 5–7 and Tables 18 and 21. Table 8 merges the previously separate OOD and black-box displays, while several retained tables are resized or rearranged.

improvement.justification: The new controlled comparisons and estimator checks make specific design choices better supported, while revised claims and limitations more accurately characterize the clean–robustness trade-off and entropy bound. These strengthen an already extensive empirical study without changing its main results. Figure 7c still leaves the entropy-bin ordering unclear, limiting that panel's interpretability.
